synthesis: Across the six sections, the same all-zeros-on-the-critical-line condition is re-encoded as equality or vanishing of zero counts, square-root-scale prime and arithmetic error, positivity of every test or coefficient, density or completeness in specified function spaces, and determinant conditions for every matrix size. The joint result is an atlas of observables with different information and quantifier structures, not a common proof mechanism linking the criteria.
source_support: The zero-count section states RH as N(T)=N0(T) or N(1/2,T)=0 for all T; the prime and arithmetic sections state equivalent square-root-scale error or cancellation and global/eventual inequalities; the positivity, function-space, and matrix sections explicitly state RH-equivalent all-test, all-coefficient, closure, and all-n determinant conditions.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compares what each representation exposes and suppresses: counts discard individual zero positions for an aggregate defect, arithmetic criteria expose discrepancies or cancellation, positivity searches for a negative direction, closure criteria search for a missing direction, and matrix criteria package the condition into nested finite tests. Their differing universal quantifiers also show why finite verification in any one representation cannot establish RH.
limits: The excerpts mostly state equivalences without deriving translations between them, so they support a representation map rather than a route from one criterion to another or a ranking of fertility. Exact constants, formulas, and some spectral details are OCR-sensitive, and the 2004 compilation cannot establish modern best bounds.
quality_reason: Accepted because six distinct parent units jointly support a concrete change-of-representation comparison and its quantifier-dependent proof burden; the synthesis explicitly avoids inferring a shared causal mechanism from co-equivalence alone.

synthesis: The source separates two logical situations that look superficially similar: its Chapter C criteria are stated as biconditionals with RH, whereas the Chapter D.3 attacks use one-way premises A that would imply RH but have themselves been disproved. Thus exact equivalence supplies an alternative target without by itself supplying a tractable attack, while a valid sufficient implication becomes unusable when its required antecedent is false.
source_support: The prime-error, positivity, and function-space units repeatedly state if-and-only-if or equivalent criteria, and the equivalence chapter warns that such criteria range from nearly trivial to deep. The unsuccessful-attacks unit explicitly characterizes its results as A implies RH with A false, then reports forbidden zeros for Turan's partial sums and failure of the proposed de Branges positivity condition.
nonparaphrase_operation: Distinguishes the proof obligations P iff RH and A implies RH together with not-A. The former changes the object on which a proof may be attempted but does not establish that P is easier; the latter preserves the implication while a counterexample removes that particular route, without refuting RH.
limits: Only the Turan and de Branges premises are explicitly blocked here, and the source neither ranks the remaining equivalences by present-day fertility nor proves that no weakened replacement could work. Exact de Branges formulas and the mollification display are extraction-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because the equivalence sections and the failed-route section jointly support a concrete logical dependency and obstruction unavailable from either group alone, while the synthesis preserves the difference between a false antecedent and a false conclusion.

synthesis: The three sections exhibit distinct epistemic strengths rather than one completed spectral construction: local CUE agreement and generic dynamical zeta models provide a statistical and role-based analogy; Hilbert-Polya asks for a specific Hermitian quantization whose eigenvalues encode zero ordinates and whose periodic orbits encode primes; Bost-Connes supplies an actual C*-dynamical system in which zeta is a partition function and its pole is a phase transition, but it addresses a different zeta feature from the required zero spectrum.
source_support: The dynamical-zeta unit gives generic spectral determinants whose zeros are system eigenvalues and periodic-orbit expansions, together with the unitary symmetry-class statistic. The Hilbert-Polya unit labels the zeta operator and underlying chaotic system as suggested targets. The Bost-Connes unit constructs the finite-adele semigroup crossed product and states partition function zeta(beta), symmetry breaking, and critical inverse temperature beta=1.
nonparaphrase_operation: Aligns and then separates the represented objects: zero spacings correspond statistically to CUE-like spectra; individual zero ordinates would have to correspond exactly to eigenvalues of the missing self-adjoint operator, with primes as periodic-orbit data; zeta(beta) and its pole correspond in the constructed C*-system to thermodynamic partition data and a phase transition. The last correspondence therefore does not discharge the middle construction obligation.
limits: Neither statistical agreement nor a generic dynamical spectral determinant identifies the required zeta Hamiltonian, and the Bost-Connes construction supplies no implication from its partition function or pole to nontrivial-zero location or RH. Periodic-orbit products and long crossed-product formulas are OCR-sensitive, and the account reflects its 2004 status.
quality_reason: Accepted because the three parents jointly support a concrete comparison of representation strength and a decisive mismatch between zero-spectrum and pole/partition-function observables; no constructed C*-system is promoted into a Hilbert-Polya solution.
